entity.agency: VT Secretary of State, Business Services Division
entity.summary: Form an LLC or corporation, or register an assumed business name (DBA), through the Secretary of State's Online Business Service Center.
entity.quote: Ready to start or register a business in Vermont? Use the Online Business Service Center to take care of your business filing needs.

state_tax.summary: Register with the Vermont Department of Taxes through myVTax. Sales and use tax and withholding each need their own business tax account.
state_tax.quote: Most businesses operating in Vermont must first register with the Vermont Department of Taxes. For Sales and Use, Meals and Rooms, or Withholding you will need a separate business tax account for each of these respective taxes.

unemployment.summary: Once you are a liable employer (for example, paying at least $1,500 in wages in a calendar quarter), you must provide unemployment insurance coverage and register with the Department of Labor.
unemployment.quote: Pays at least $1,500 in gross wages during any calendar quarter in either the current or the preceding calendar year, regardless of the number of employees;

workers_comp.agency: VT Department of Labor, Workers' Compensation Program
workers_comp.summary: You must buy workers' comp if you hire one or more full- or part-time employees in Vermont. Sole proprietors and partners of unincorporated businesses don't have to cover themselves; corporate officers can opt out only with Department approval.
workers_comp.quote: You hire one or more employees on a full or part time basis in Vermont, or

residential_building.name: Residential Contractor Registration
residential_building.agency: VT Secretary of State, Office of Professional Regulation (OPR)
residential_building.covers: Anyone contracting directly with a homeowner for residential construction (building, remodeling, repair, painting, paving, roofing, weatherization, heating, plumbing, electrical, etc.) on buildings with four or fewer units.
residential_building.threshold: Jobs over $10,000 including labor and materials.
prerequisites: Register with OPR before contracting for a job over $10,000
Liability insurance of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate (certificate uploaded with application)
Written contract required for jobs over $10,000
residential_building.insurance: Liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate.
residential_building.summary: Vermont requires residential contractors to register with OPR before contracting with a homeowner for work over $10,000. You must carry liability insurance and use a written contract. Subcontractors hired by another contractor don't need to register.
residential_building.quote: A person shall register with the Office of Professional Regulation prior to contracting with a homeowner to perform residential construction in exchange for consideration of more than $10,000.00, including labor and materials.

evidence.quote: A person registered under this chapter shall maintain minimum liability insurance coverage in the amount of $1,000,000.00 per occurrence and $2,000,000.00 aggregate

A person registered under this chapter shall execute a written contract prior to receiving a deposit or commencing residential construction work if the estimated value of the labor and materials exceeds $10,000.00.
Yes, you will be required to upload a copy of your certificate of insurance with your initial and biennial renewal applications.

commercial_building.agency: VT Secretary of State, Office of Professional Regulation
commercial_building.covers: Commercial-only contractors do not register with OPR; they must register if they take a residential job of $10,000 or more.
commercial_building.summary: Vermont has no state general contractor license for commercial work. Trade licenses (electrical, plumbing, gas) still apply.
commercial_building.quote: No; but you are required to register if you accept a residential job where the estimated value is $10,000 or more inclusive of labor and materials.

electrical.name: Master Electrician and Journeyman Electrician licenses
electrical.agency: VT Department of Public Safety, Division of Fire Safety (Electricians' Licensing Board)
electrical.covers: Anyone installing, replacing or repairing electrical installations; a master electrician may run an electrical business and employ other licensees.
prerequisites: Journeyman: complete an apprenticeship verified by the Vermont Apprenticeship Council (or equivalent training) and pass an exam
Master: licensed as a journeyman for at least two years (or comparable experience) and pass an exam
electrical.summary: Vermont licenses electricians at the state level. Journeymen complete an apprenticeship and pass an exam; masters need two years as a licensed journeyman and another exam. A master electrician can run an electrical business.
electrical.quote: Any person who installs, replaces, or repairs any electrical installation except as provided in sections 882 and 910 of this title, without first obtaining an appropriate license under this subchapter

evidence.quote: have been licensed as a journeyman electrician under this chapter for at least two years
provide verification by the Vermont Apprenticeship Council of completion of an apprenticeship in electrical wiring that included both instruction and practice in work processes
may employ other persons licensed under this chapter or electrician’s helpers to perform work in connection with electrical installations under his or her direction

plumbing.name: Master Plumber and Journeyman Plumber licenses
plumbing.agency: VT Department of Public Safety, Division of Fire Safety (Plumber's Examining Board)
plumbing.covers: All plumbing and specialty work in Vermont, except an owner working in their own owner-occupied single-family home.
prerequisites: Journeyman: plumbing apprenticeship verified by the Vermont Apprenticeship Council (or equivalent) and pass an exam
Master: hold a journeyman plumber license for at least 12 months (or equivalent) and pass an exam
plumbing.summary: All plumbing work must be done by state-licensed plumbers. Journeymen complete an apprenticeship and pass an exam; masters need 12 months as a licensed journeyman and pass another exam.
plumbing.quote: All plumbing and specialty work performed in Vermont shall be performed by persons licensed under this chapter except that a license shall not be required for the following types of work:

evidence.quote: of having held a valid journeyman plumber’s license under this chapter for at least 12 months
apprenticeship in plumbing that includes both instruction and practice in work processes as verified by the Vermont Apprenticeship Council

mechanical.name: Natural and Propane Gas certifications; Oil Burner Installer certification
mechanical.agency: VT Department of Public Safety, Division of Fire Safety
mechanical.covers: Individuals who install, inspect or service propane or natural gas systems (and oil burner installers). Vermont has no general HVAC contractor license.
prerequisites: Gas certification training (e.g., NPGA CETP or PEP) and the state education module
mechanical.summary: Vermont has no general HVAC/mechanical contractor license, but anyone installing or servicing propane or natural gas systems must hold a Division of Fire Safety gas certification, and oil burner installers are certified too. Heating work for homeowners over the threshold also needs residential contractor registration.
mechanical.quote: All individuals engaged in the inspection, installation, and service of Propane (LP) or Natural Gas systems must be certified as required under the Vermont Fire and Building Safety Code.

evidence.quote: If you are applying for a new license or certification, or renewing an existing license or certification after July 1, 2021, you are required to complete the education module.

roofing.name: Residential Contractor Registration (covers roofing)
roofing.agency: VT Secretary of State, Office of Professional Regulation
roofing.covers: Roofing is listed as residential construction; no separate roofing license.
prerequisites: Residential contractor registration and liability insurance for homeowner jobs over $10,000
roofing.insurance: Same liability insurance as residential contractor registration.
roofing.summary: Vermont has no separate roofing license. Roofing for homeowners is covered by residential contractor registration when the job is over $10,000.
roofing.quote: includes interior and exterior construction, renovation, and repair; painting; paving; roofing; weatherization; installation or repair of heating, plumbing, solar, electrical, water, or wastewater systems

evidence.quote: A person shall register with the Office of Professional Regulation prior to contracting with a homeowner to perform residential construction in exchange for consideration of more than $10,000.00, including labor and materials.

pesticide.name: Pesticide Company License and Commercial Applicator Certification
pesticide.agency: VT Agency of Agriculture, Food and Markets
pesticide.covers: Businesses and applicators using pesticides on others' property (pest control, lawn/weed control, tree spraying).
prerequisites: Pass the pesticide applicator certification exam
pesticide.summary: Using pesticides commercially requires a Pesticide Company License for the business and commercial applicator certification (by exam) for applicators, issued by the Agency of Agriculture.
pesticide.quote: used pesticides without first obtaining the appropriate company license or applicator certificate;

evidence.quote: Examination fee for dealer licenses and applicator certification

asbestos.name: Asbestos abatement company license; asbestos worker/supervisor licenses
asbestos.agency: VT Department of Health, Asbestos and Lead Regulatory Program
asbestos.covers: Removing asbestos-containing materials before renovation or demolition; also an asbestos assessment by a licensed inspector before renovating or demolishing.
prerequisites: Up-to-date training from a Health Department-accredited training provider
Abatement permit application filed before each project
asbestos.summary: Asbestos must be removed by a Vermont-licensed asbestos abatement company, and workers need accredited training before licensing. Before any renovation or demolition, confirm an asbestos assessment was done by a Vermont-licensed inspector.
asbestos.quote: Asbestos-containing materials must be removed by a Vermont-licensed asbestos abatement company before the renovation or demolition.

evidence.quote: Asbestos and lead contractors must have up-to-date training from an accredited training provider before they can be licensed to work in Vermont.
No one may renovate or demolish a building or other structure or a portion of a it without first getting confirmation from the owner that an asbestos assessment has been completed

lead_rrp.name: Lead-Safe Renovation, Repair, Painting and Maintenance (RRPM) license
lead_rrp.covers: Workers and businesses disturbing painted surfaces above small thresholds in buildings built before 1978.
prerequisites: RRPM training and a Vermont RRPM license for the individual and the business
lead_rrp.summary: Vermont runs its own lead-safe program (RRPM) instead of EPA. Workers and businesses doing RRPM work on pre-1978 buildings must be trained and licensed by the Health Department.
lead_rrp.quote: The Health Department oversees compliance with the Vermont Renovation, Repair, Painting and Maintenance (RRPM) regulations and licenses individuals and businesses that perform RRPM work.

evidence.quote: Because lead is hazardous, workers must be trained and licensed to use lead-safe practices when working on painted surfaces in buildings built before 1978.

other.name: Boilers and Pressure Vessels licensing
other.summary: The Division of Fire Safety licenses and certifies trade groups including boilers and pressure vessels, gas installers and oil burner installers.
other.quote: The Division of Fire Safety administers licensing and certification of trade groups to maintain professionals at a high level of technical knowledge.
